svg.title: Temperature versus heat added to water
svg.desc: Temperature versus energy added per gram, ΔQ/m, starting with ice at −20 °C. The ice warms to 0 °C after 10 cal/g. The temperature stays at 0 °C while the ice melts, absorbing 79.8 cal/g, to about 90 cal/g. The liquid water then warms to 100 °C, reached at about 190 cal/g. The temperature stays at 100 °C while the water boils, absorbing 539 cal/g, to about 729 cal/g. The steam then warms to 120 °C at about 738 cal/g. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Added heat changes phase while temperature stays on a plateau
Book heat capacities and latent heats at about 1 atm. Playback gives each stage equal time, not equal
heat input. Bars show mass fractions, not phase volumes; no heat loss is included.
